lines.japanese: それから小一時間が過ぎて、俺たちは本当にメンマのお言葉に甘えていた。
lines.english: Nearly an hour later, we were still there, taking Menma’s invitation to linger entirely at face value.

lines.japanese: すでに食器を下げられた俺たちの隣りでは、日曜の柳木原を満喫してきた３０前後くらいの男女が、クリアカップのビールをすすりながら小声で語らっていた。
lines.english: Our dishes had long since been cleared. Beside us, a couple around thirty, fresh from a Sunday out in Yanagihara, sipped beer from clear plastic cups and spoke in low voices.

lines.japanese: カウンター席には茶色い頭の大学生が三人並んで、厄介な先輩をいかにしてクリスマスパーティーに来させずやり過ごすかのプランを練っている。
lines.english: Three brown-haired college students lined the counter, devising a plan to get through their Christmas party without one particularly troublesome upperclassman showing up.

lines.japanese: 鳴が面白がるから、俺はエージに騙されて請けおった、泣きたくなるようなハズレ仕事をいくつか語った。
lines.english: Naru found them funny, so I told her about a few of the nightmare jobs Eiji had conned me into taking.

lines.japanese: 新興宗教のサクラとして畳の広間に座らされ、腹まで髭の伸びた仙人みたいなじいさんの説法を八時間延々聞かされたこととか。
lines.english: Like the time I was hired as a shill for some new religion, planted in a straw-matted hall and subjected to an eight-hour sermon from an old hermit whose beard reached his stomach.

lines.japanese: ハプニングバーの定例イベントで、ベネツィアの仮面舞踏会みたいな扮装をさせられてＳＭ嬢のアシスタントを務めたこととか。
lines.english: Or the time a regular event at a swingers’ club had me dressed for a Venetian masquerade and working as a dominatrix’s assistant.

lines.japanese: 市民団体と称する（ぜってー嘘だ）イカれたおっさん達のワゴンに乗せられ、空港拡張工事の反対デモに参加させられたこととか。しかもその後、あやうく本気で入隊させられそうになったこととか。
lines.english: Or the time a band of lunatics calling themselves a citizens' group—which was a goddamn lie—bundled me into their van to protest an airport expansion, then nearly recruited me for real afterward.

lines.japanese: （な、俺がエージの電話から逃げまわる気持ちが、よーく分かるだろ？）
lines.english: (See? Now you understand perfectly well why I spend my life running from Eiji's calls.)

lines.japanese: 鳴の方は、一家四人で暮らしていたころのあったかいホームドラマや、アムステルダムの日本人学校で巻きおこした小さなドタバタ劇なんかを語った。やつは俺と逆で、最近の話をあんまりしなかった。
lines.english: Naru, for her part, told warm family stories from when all four of them still lived together, and comic scrapes from the Japanese school in Amsterdam. Unlike me, she said very little about anything recent.

lines.japanese: 「はー、日曜の夜ってアレですよねー」
lines.english: “Sunday nights have that certain something, don't they?”

lines.japanese: ガードレールの向こうへ首を曲げていた鳴が、出し抜けに呟いた。
lines.english: Naru murmured it out of nowhere, neck craned toward the far side of the guardrail.

lines.japanese: こいつのいきなりにももう慣れたけど、ただ、いまのは俺がたまたまテーブルに乗りだして頬杖をついてなかったら、クルマの走行音と排気ガスに呑まれて聞きのがしていたぐらいの声だった。
lines.english: I was used to her non sequiturs by now. Still, if I hadn’t happened to be leaning across the table with my cheek in one hand, this one would have vanished beneath the traffic noise and exhaust fumes.

lines.japanese: 「あー？　なに、アレって」
lines.english: “Yeah? What certain something?”

lines.japanese: 俺はあえて気だるげに訊いた。
lines.english: I made a point of sounding languid.

lines.japanese: 「えー、ほら、祭りのあとって言うんですかー」
lines.english: “You know. The feeling after the festival's over.”

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: そういうアレか……。
lines.english: So that kind of something...

lines.japanese: 生活サイクルが特殊な俺にも、月曜日の足音が憂鬱だった時期はある。同情を禁じえない。俺はあくびを呑みこんで言った。
lines.english: Even with my peculiar schedule, there had been a time when the sound of Monday bearing down on me filled me with gloom. I couldn’t help but sympathize. I swallowed a yawn.

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、明日からまた一週間ガッコだもんな。がんばれよ」
lines.english: “You've got a whole week of school starting tomorrow. Good luck.”

lines.japanese: やつは車道を眺めたまま、しかしハイとは答えなかった。
lines.english: She kept watching the roadway, but made no answer.

lines.japanese: 「あのー、ドラさんってー、学生時代はやっぱり不良のひとだったんですかー」
lines.english: “Um, Dra... were you a delinquent back when you were a student too?”

lines.japanese: 「え、なに、やっぱりって」
lines.english: “What do you mean, ‘too’?”

lines.japanese: 「やー、実は私も、最近わりと不良なんですよー」
lines.english: “Well, the truth is, I've become rather a delinquent myself lately.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、『も』じゃねえよ。ひとの話聞けよ」
lines.english: “Don’t ‘me too’ me. Listen when people talk.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、そもそもの始まりは、残暑がようやく過ぎさろうとしていた秋の日のことなんですけどー」
lines.english: “It all began one autumn day, just as the lingering heat of summer was finally passing...”

lines.japanese: 「ちょちょちょ、勝手に時間戻すなっつの。ナウ俺の話を聞けよ」
lines.english: “Whoa, whoa, whoa. No unauthorized flashbacks. I'm talking *now.*”

lines.japanese: 「その日ー、珍しく私、座れたんですよー」
lines.english: “That morning, most unusually, I got a seat.”

lines.japanese: 「──あ？　なにが。便所か。いつもは立ってしてんのか」
lines.english: “—Huh? On what, the toilet? You usually do it standing up?”

lines.japanese: 「あーいえ、朝の通学電車です。柳木原行き急行列車です。もー、ちょー満員なんですけどー、ほんとその日はたまたま運良く私の前が空きましてー」
lines.english: “No, on my morning train to school. The express to Yanagihara. It's always packed, but that day, by pure luck, the seat in front of me opened up.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “Right.”

lines.japanese: 「でー、座るじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “So naturally, I sat down.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、空いてりゃ座るわなそりゃ」
lines.english: “Well, yeah. Seat opens up, you sit in it.”

lines.japanese: 「でー、グーグー寝るじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “And naturally, I fell asleep snoring.”

lines.japanese: 「くーくー寝るじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “I slept like a little angel, I mean.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、べつに可愛らしく言いなおさなくていいけど」
lines.english: “You don’t have to make it cuter the second time.”

lines.japanese: 「でー、目覚めるじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “And naturally, I woke up.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「そしたらもー、びっくりですよー？　けっこーな時間寝てたはずなのにー、窓の外を見やればなんと、眠りに就く前と寸分違わぬ風景が！」
lines.english: “Imagine my surprise. I must have slept for ages, and yet when I looked out the window, the landscape was identical in every particular to the one I'd seen before I drifted off!”

lines.japanese: 「え、なんだよ。なんだよソレちょっと。おまえ、いきなり怪談始めんなよ。おしっこちびっちゃうだろ」
lines.english: “Wait, what? What's this all of a sudden? Don't start telling ghost stories without warning. I'll piss myself.”

lines.japanese: 「あーいえいえ、実はただ寝過ごしてただけなんですけどー。ええ、電車とっくに終点着いて折りかえしてたんですねー」
lines.english: “Oh, no, no. I'd simply slept past my stop. The train had reached the terminus ages ago and was already on its way back.”

lines.japanese: 「んーだよソレ、てめ、そんな普通のオチかよ。あんまちびらせんじゃねえぞコラ。パンツ洗わせんぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “That's it? What kind of ordinary punch line is that? Don't scare the piss out of me for nothing. I'll make you wash my underwear, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「でもー、それって確実に遅刻じゃないですかー」
lines.english: “But that meant I was unquestionably late.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　ああ、そりゃなぁ。そんだけガン寝してたらなぁ」
lines.english: “Well, yeah. You slept like the dead.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、それはもう慌てて飛びおりて、柳木原行きに乗りなおすじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “So naturally, I leapt off in a panic and boarded another train for Yanagihara.”

lines.japanese: 「ところがですよー、ほら私、焦ってたじゃないですかー。間違って変な電車に乗っちゃったみたいでー」
lines.english: “But you see, I was panicking. Apparently I got on a rather strange train by mistake.”

lines.japanese: 「なに、変な電車って」
lines.english: “What do you mean, a strange train?”

lines.japanese: 「えーと、そうですねー、さしづめ迷える美少女をさらなる困惑の辺境へといざなう銀河超鈍行とでも申しましょうか」
lines.english: “Let us call it the Galactic Ultra-Local, bearing a lost young beauty onward to yet more bewildering frontiers.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、要するにアレだろ。下りの快速から上り快速に乗りかえたつもりが、間違って下りの各駅に乗っちゃったんだろ」
lines.english: “Meaning you thought you'd changed from the outbound express to the inbound express, but got on an outbound local instead.”

lines.japanese: 「まー、かいつまんで言うとそういうことですけどー」
lines.english: “Well, if one must condense it, yes.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、かいつままなくてもそういうことだろ。つかソレ、ぜんぜん変な電車じゃねーじゃん。むしろおまえが変じゃん」
lines.english: “That's what happened whether you condense it or not. Nothing was strange about the train. *You're* the strange one.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、まー、古くから諺にも、急いてはことを仕損じるなんて申しますように」
lines.english: “Well, as the ancient proverb says, haste makes waste.”

lines.japanese: 鳴はてのひらを体の前にふたつドンと立てて、こっちの言葉を防御した。俺は右手一本でその壁をひと薙ぎする。
lines.english: Naru planted both palms upright before her with a thump, raising a wall against my words. I swept it aside with one hand.

lines.japanese: 「あぁー」
lines.english: “Aaah...”

lines.japanese: 壁と共に流れてゆく小娘の体。ほんと面白ぇやつだ。
lines.english: The little girl drifted away with her wall. God, she was entertaining.

lines.japanese: 「で。結局その日は大遅刻か」
lines.english: “So? You ended up spectacularly late?”

lines.japanese: 「やー、まー、遅刻と言いますか……ねぇ？」
lines.english: “Well, it wasn't so much that I was late... you know?”

lines.japanese: 鳴は文末を省略し、意味ありげなツラでその空欄の解を誘う。たしかに、あくびが出そうなほど簡単なクイズではあるけれど。
lines.english: Naru left the sentence unfinished and gave me a meaningful look, inviting me to fill in the blank. Admittedly, the puzzle was so easy it nearly made me yawn.

lines.japanese: 「サボったんだ。丸一日」
lines.english: “You skipped the whole day.”

lines.japanese: 俺はことさら平板な調子で答えた。鳴は唇をおかしな形に巻きこみながら、こくんと一回うなずいた。
lines.english: I answered with studied flatness. Naru curled her lips inward into a funny little shape and nodded once.

lines.japanese: 「やー、初めはそこまで大掛かりなことをするつもりではなかったんですよー」
lines.english: “I hadn't intended anything quite so drastic at first.”

lines.japanese: 「ただあのー……ほら、ちょっとの遅刻は焦りますけどー、ダイナミックな遅刻ってかえって居直りたくなるじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “It's just... a little lateness makes you panic, but once you're *spectacularly* late, don't you start feeling strangely defiant?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、それはあるな」
lines.english: “Ah. Yeah, that happens.”

lines.japanese: 「ねー、ですからそのときの私もー、ふたたび上り電車に乗りなおして柳木原へ向かうころには、ロングシートの真ん中に座ってそれはもう悠々閑々ですよ」
lines.english: “Exactly. By the time I boarded yet another inbound train to Yanagihara, I was enthroned in the middle of a bench seat, perfectly carefree.”

lines.japanese: 「おう、オフピーク通学じゃん。混雑率緩和に貢献してんじゃん。国土交通省、大喜びだな」
lines.english: “Hey, off-peak commuting. Doing your part to ease congestion. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport must've been thrilled.”

lines.japanese: 「はいー、しかもあえて快速・急行をスルーして、わざわざ各駅停車の旅ですよー」
lines.english: “Yes. I even let the expresses and rapid trains pass so I could take a journey on the local.”

lines.japanese: 「うお、マジかよ。どんだけだよ。おまえ、どんだけいい日旅立ちだよ」
lines.english: “Whoa, seriously? Look at you, turning it into your own ‘perfect day to hit the rails’ commercial.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、もー、乗車率５０％未満の車窓から眺める景観は、いつもの通いあきた道のりとはとても思えない新鮮な感覚を──」
lines.english: “The scenery from a train at less than fifty percent capacity made the same old route I thought I’d seen enough of for a lifetime feel wonderfully fresh—”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なに」
lines.english: “Huh? What?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、あれかー、さっき階段でドラさん言ってたのー」
lines.english: “Oh. So that's what you were talking about on the stairs earlier.”

lines.japanese: 鳴はいつもより一回りほどでっかく口を開け、しばし地上を走る地下鉄の短い旅情に耽っているみたいだった。
lines.english: Naru's mouth opened one size wider than usual, and for a while she seemed lost in the brief romance of a subway journey above ground.

lines.japanese: やっぱこいつ、俺に似てるのかも。
lines.english: Maybe she really was like me.

lines.japanese: 「あのードラさん、いま入ったニュースなんですけどー。往来での座りこみは感心できないので、街頭トリップには各駅停車の旅がお勧めらしいです」
lines.english: “Dra, this just in. Because sitting down in a public thoroughfare is frowned upon, the local train is apparently the recommended venue for urban tripping.”

lines.japanese: 「っせえな、いんだよ。適正場所には個人差があんだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up. Ideal tripping grounds vary by individual.”

lines.japanese: 俺は頬杖ついて軽口を返した。鳴はしばしポケーッともの思いに暮れたが、俺を待たせていることに気付いて話を続けた。
lines.english: Cheek in hand, I tossed the joke back. Naru drifted vacantly into thought, then noticed she had left me waiting and resumed her story.

lines.japanese: 「やー、そのあと柳木原の駅に着いてー、学校に行ってはみたんですよー。でもー、朝と違ってなんかすっごくしーんとしててー……えーと、あの感じ分かりますー？」
lines.english: “After that, I reached Yanagihara Station and did try going to school. But unlike in the morning, it was all so terribly silent... Do you know that feeling?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、まー、分かんなくはねーかな。ちょっと入りづれーよな」
lines.english: “Yeah. I guess I do. Makes it hard to walk in.”

lines.japanese: 「はいー。というわけなのでー、校舎には昼休みのどさくさに紛れて潜りこむことにしましてー、ひとまずどこかでこっそり時間を潰すことにしたんですねー」
lines.english: “Exactly. So I decided to slip into the building amid the confusion of lunch break. Until then, I would quietly kill time somewhere.”

lines.japanese: 「でー、ファーストフードの店でも入ろうと、街の中をこそこそ歩くじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “So naturally, I crept through town looking for a fast-food place.”

lines.japanese: 「そしたら意外に、私と同じ制服の子がちらほら散見されましてー、なんかこー『あれっ？』て拍子抜けした気分になってくるわけですよー」
lines.english: “But to my surprise, I kept spotting girls in my own school uniform around town. It rather took the wind out of my sails. I thought, ‘Oh. Is that all?’”

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: まあ、そうだろう。是非はともかく、事実としてそういう時代だからな。
lines.english: Well, yes. Whatever anyone thought of it, those were the times.

lines.japanese: 「そんなときにこう、自転車屋さんの軒先に並んだ、背もたれ付きの赤い自転車が目に入ってしまいまして。ええ、もう、ついうっかり」
lines.english: “Then a red bicycle with a backrest, displayed outside a bike shop, caught my eye. And, well, before I knew it...”

lines.japanese: 「はいもう、たちまち風を切って、すいすいと走りたい衝動に駆られてしまったわけですね」
lines.english: “I was seized by the desire to fly along with the wind in my face.”

lines.japanese: 「わけですね、って、いや、その繋がりはよく分かんねーけど──」
lines.english: “‘Seized by the desire,’ huh? I don't quite see how one thing led to—”

lines.japanese: 「──あ、いやまあ、分かるっちゃ分かるような？　ん、どうだ……？」
lines.english: “—No, wait. Maybe I kind of do? Hm. Do I...?”

lines.japanese: 共感できそうな気がして、俺は腕を組んで考えてみた。
lines.english: Feeling as if I might understand, I folded my arms and considered it.

lines.japanese: 教室の隅でいつもひっそり毛づくろいしていたペンギンが、檻から抜けだしたそこで出逢ったもの。それは青空へはばたくための真っ赤な翼──なんて、おとぎ話風にしてみれば分かりやいかもしれない。
lines.english: The penguin who had always preened quietly in a corner of the classroom escaped her cage and found, waiting beyond it, a pair of crimson wings made to soar into the blue—put it like a fairy tale and perhaps it made sense.

lines.japanese: 「そんで、どーしたの」
lines.english: “So what did you do?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、こう、それなりに長い時間どうしたものかと悩みまして──」
lines.english: “Well, I agonized over it for quite some time—”

lines.japanese: 鳴は片手で膝を抱え、もう一方の手の甲に小さな顎を載せた。作品名、考える鳴。
lines.english: Naru hugged one knee and set her little chin on the back of her other hand. Title: *Naru, Thinking.*

lines.japanese: やつは数秒間ロダンの彫刻みたいに固まってみせたが、不意に背筋を伸ばして顔を上げた。
lines.english: She held her Rodin pose for several seconds, then abruptly straightened and raised her head.

lines.japanese: 「──けっきょく母の名を騙って学校に電話しました。娘が風邪をひいたという設定で」
lines.english: “—and in the end, I called the school pretending to be my mother. I told them her daughter had a cold.”

lines.japanese: 「ほー、演技派女優。いい度胸してんじゃん」
lines.english: “Well, look at the great actress. You've got nerve.”

lines.japanese: 「とんでもないです、とんでもないです」
lines.english: “Oh, hardly. Hardly.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は顔を地面に向けて、つむじの前で手刀を左右に振った。
lines.english: Naru bowed her head and chopped one hand briskly back and forth above her crown.

lines.japanese: 「も、ぜんぜんです。心臓ばくばくでした。喉からからでした。頭の中で何度も復唱した台詞は軽く四回噛みました」
lines.english: “Not at all. My heart was pounding, my throat was bone-dry, and I tripped over the lines I'd rehearsed in my head at least four times.”

lines.japanese: 「マジで。おまえソレ、よくバレなかったな」
lines.english: “Seriously? How the hell did they not catch you?”

lines.japanese: 「ですよねー。両親離婚してますからその辺も心配だったんですけどー、緊張してたのが馬鹿みたいに、あっさり『お大事に』でがちゃんですよ」
lines.english: “I know. My parents are divorced, so I was worried about details like that too. But all that anxiety was for nothing: they just said, ‘Take care,’ and—click.”

lines.japanese: 「ですからー、受話器を置いて電話ボックスから出た瞬間、いつの間にやら掻いていたヤなカンジの汗がすーっと引いていきましてー」
lines.english: “The instant I hung up and stepped out of the phone booth, all that clammy sweat I hadn't even noticed working up simply drained away.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、なんと言いますかねこう、罪悪感以上の解放感がふわぁーって押しよせてきたわけですよ」
lines.english: “How shall I put it? A rush of freedom, bigger than any guilt, came sweeping over me.”

lines.japanese: 「そのとき気付いたんですよねー。あー私、自分で思ってた以上に学校嫌いだったんだなーって」
lines.english: “That was when I realized. Oh—I hated school much more than I'd ever thought.”

lines.japanese: そんなありふれたことを、やつがいかにも照れくさそうに言うもんだから、つい俺も釣られた。
lines.english: It was the most ordinary confession in the world. But she made it so sheepishly that she drew one from me too.

lines.japanese: 「同じ同じ。俺も長期のバイトとか、えれー苦手。休憩時間なに話しゃいいとか分かんねーし」
lines.english: “Same here. I'm terrible at long-term jobs. I never know what to talk about on breaks.”

lines.japanese: 「えー」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 俺の苦そうな顔を見て、鳴は不満げな声をあげた。
lines.english: The pained look on my face drew a disgruntled sound from Naru.

lines.japanese: 「なんでですかー。ドラさんだったら、いつも私とかパルさんと話すときみたいに、このやろーとかブラックホールとか、しょーもないこと喋ってればいいじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “Why? You could talk the way you always do with Paru and me. Call people assholes, go on about black holes—your usual nonsense.”

lines.japanese: 「アホかおまえ。現場に新人入ってきて、いきなりブッ殺すぞコノヤロウとか、俺の肛門は宇宙だとか言いだしたら引くだろ。むしろソッコーお引き取り願うだろ」
lines.english: “Are you stupid? New guy shows up at a work site and immediately announces, ‘I’ll fucking kill you, asshole,’ and ‘my asshole is the universe’—people back away. Hell, they send him straight back out the door.”

lines.japanese: 「つーかさ、おまえだって学校じゃ猫かぶってんじゃねーの」
lines.english: “Besides, don’t you put on a good-girl act at school too?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、まー、浮かないよう気を付けてはいますけどー。どーなんでしょうねー」
lines.english: “Well, I try not to stick out. Whether it works is another matter.”

lines.japanese: 俺たちは苦い顔を見合わせ、仕事帰りのサラリーマンみたいに小さな溜息をついた。
lines.english: We exchanged bitter looks and let out little sighs like office workers on the way home.

lines.japanese: 「いや、その点さ、たまに街でばったり会うだけの仲は簡単だよな」
lines.english: “That's the nice thing about people you only happen to run into around town. Those relationships are easy.”

lines.japanese: 何年も夜の柳木原を歩いていれば、そりゃいろんなやつに出会う。何度もすれ違ってるうち、名前や素性を知らないどころかほとんど言葉も交わさないまま、なんとなく顔見知りになっていたやつも少なくない。
lines.english: Walk the streets of Yanagihara at night for years and naturally you run into all kinds of people. More than a few had become familiar faces through repeated crossings, though we knew nothing of each other’s names or lives and had barely exchanged a word.

lines.japanese: 通りの角に立つ飲み屋の呼び込み。閉まった銀行の前に座る占い師。駅前で露店を広げる雑誌売りのじいさん。自販機の陰に潜んだコールガール。明け方まで美味い飯を食わせてくれるラーメン屋、とその常連客たち。
lines.english: The bar tout stationed on the corner. The fortune-teller outside a shuttered bank. The old man laying out magazines for sale by the station. The call girl tucked behind a vending machine. The ramen man who served good food until dawn, and all his regulars.

lines.japanese: そういう特殊な関係下では、（極端な話）次に通りすぎたときお互いなんとなく目を合わせなかったとしてもとくに問題はない。むしろ名前やらメアドやらを無闇に尋ねてはならないような磁場が形成される。
lines.english: Inside those peculiar relationships, it hardly mattered if—to take the extreme case—you passed each other next time and somehow neither of you made eye contact. If anything, a kind of force field formed between you, one in which casually asking for a name or email address felt forbidden.

lines.japanese: そういう磁場を通しての交流は、互いに肩肘を張る必要がない。不都合が生じればいつでも気兼ねなくフェイドアウトできるからだ。
lines.english: In relationships conducted through that force field, neither person had to posture or strain. If things grew inconvenient, either could fade out at any time without hard feelings.

lines.japanese: 近付いてないから遠ざかってもいい。人付き合いにおいて、この曖昧な距離感はとても合理的だと思う──鷲介に言ったら鼻で笑われたけど。
lines.english: If you had never come close, you were free to drift apart. In human relationships, I found that ambiguous distance perfectly rational—though Shusuke had snorted when I told him so.

lines.japanese: 「でも学校だと、なかなかそーゆーわけ行かないもんな」
lines.english: “But school doesn't really let you do that.”

lines.japanese: 「あはー」
lines.english: “Ah-ha.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は俺の同情ヅラを見てだらしなく笑った。
lines.english: Naru saw the sympathy on my face and gave me a lazy, lopsided grin.

lines.japanese: 「やー、それでもやっぱり、学校は休んじゃいかんですよねー」
lines.english: “Even so, skipping school is wrong, isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「そうかあ？　いや、全然いんじゃねーの。いや、全然アリだろ。つか、そんなんで悩んじゃうなんておまえ、悪りい意味で真面目なんだよ。むしろ、若いうちにそーゆー社会勉強しといてぜってー良かったって」
lines.english: “Is it? I think it's completely fine. More than fine. Agonizing over it just means you're serious in all the wrong ways. If anything, getting that kind of life experience while you're young was definitely good for you.”

lines.japanese: 「つーかさあ、いまどき親とか教師だって大して怒りゃしねーだろ、そんな、サボリの一日や二日ぐれーじゃさ」
lines.english: “Besides, parents and teachers these days won't get that angry over a day or two of cutting class.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、二ヵ月です」
lines.english: “No. Two months.”

lines.japanese: 「べつに大差ねーって、二日でも二ヵ月でも──」
lines.english: “Hardly any difference. Two days, two months—”

lines.japanese: 「──って、えええ、ふた月も休んだのかよ」
lines.english: “—Wait, what? You skipped *two months?*”

lines.japanese: 「はー。と言いますか、あれ以来、現在進行形なんですけどー」
lines.english: “Yes. Or rather, I'm still doing it.”

lines.japanese: 「え。それってつまり」
lines.english: “Wait. So you mean...”

lines.japanese: 「まー、いわゆるひとつの登校拒否ですよね」
lines.english: “I suppose you'd call it school refusal.”

lines.japanese: 「引きますよねー、やっぱり。だから今まで言えなかったんですけどー」
lines.english: “That puts you off, doesn't it? I thought it would. That's why I never told you.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや……引きゃーしねーけどさ……」
lines.english: “No, it doesn't... Surprised me, that's all...”

lines.japanese: そんなんはべつに森里とか香田とか、他にもまあ、どっかに例がある話だ。経験者は語る。
lines.english: It wasn’t as though hers was an unheard-of case. There was Morisato, Koda, and doubtless someone else somewhere. Take it from a man of experience.

lines.japanese: 「ま、でもちょっと驚いた。なんつーかアレ……ほら、おまえいつも制服だし？」
lines.english: “It's just... you know. You're always in uniform.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、父や家政婦さんの目もありますしー」
lines.english: “My father and the housekeeper might see me.”

lines.japanese: 「家政婦さん」
lines.english: “The housekeeper.”

lines.japanese: ……んだよ、やっぱお嬢じゃん。
lines.english: ...Come on. She *was* a rich girl.

lines.japanese: 「それに一応、ちゃんと登校しなきゃとは思いながら家を出るんですよー、毎朝ー」
lines.english: “Besides, I leave the house every morning fully intending to go to school.”

lines.japanese: 「でも学校が近付いてくるにつれてー、んーもう一日ぐらいもう一日だけって感じでこー、延び延びになってしまいましてー……ねー、もー、これどうしましょう」
lines.english: “But the closer I get, the more I think, well, perhaps one more day. Just one. And so it keeps stretching on... What am I supposed to do?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、どうしましょったってなあ」
lines.english: “You ask me that, but...”

lines.japanese: 俺は後ろ頭をがしがし掻いた。本来なら男として、年長者として、やつを戒めるクールな至言のひとつでも叩きつけるべきなのかもしれない。
lines.english: I scratched hard at the back of my head. As a man and her elder, perhaps I ought to lay one cool, hard maxim on her and set her straight.

lines.japanese: だけど、なあ？　この臆病な女と似たり寄ったりな俺が、自分のこと棚に上げて奇麗事をぬかすだなんて、おまえや鷲介は片腹痛いと顔をしかめるはずだ。違うか？
lines.english: But come on. A coward much like her, setting his own failures aside while he preached pretty ideals? You and Shusuke would both wince at the absurdity. Wouldn't you?

lines.japanese: 「つーかさあ」
lines.english: “Besides...”

lines.japanese: 俺は爪のあいだに挟まったわずかなフケを見下ろし、短い息ひとつで吹きとばした。
lines.english: I looked at the fleck of dandruff beneath one nail and blew it away with a short breath.

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、ふた月連続ってソレ、さすがに親バレしてんじゃねーの」
lines.english: “If this has gone on for two whole months, your parents have got to know by now.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、そうですよねー。いくらなんでも学校から連絡行ってますよねー」
lines.english: “Mm. You would think the school has contacted them by this point.”

lines.japanese: 鳴はさして困っているようには見えない（実際はどうだろう）口調で、すらすらと言った。
lines.english: Naru said it smoothly, in a voice that did not sound especially troubled—though who knew how she truly felt.

lines.japanese: 「しかもこないだ私ー、勤労感謝の日だってこと忘れて、祝日に制服着て家出たりしてますしねー」
lines.english: “And the other day I forgot it was Labor Thanksgiving Day and left home in my uniform on a national holiday.”

lines.japanese: ああ……そういや着てたな。なんだアレ、補習じゃなかったのか。
lines.english: Ah... right, she had been wearing it. So that hadn't been remedial school.

lines.japanese: いや、それよりも、いまの話で引っかかったのは……。
lines.english: But more than that, something in what she'd just said caught at me.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ」
lines.english: “Listen.”

lines.japanese: 俺は非難がましくならないよう努めて尋ねた。
lines.english: I took care to keep accusation out of my voice.

lines.japanese: 「え、おまえのとーちゃん、どんななの」
lines.english: “What kind of man is your dad?”

lines.japanese: 「はー、貿易会社を営んでる立派なひとですよー。社会的には尊敬に値するんじゃないですかねー」
lines.english: “Oh, a fine man who runs a trading company. From society's point of view, I imagine he deserves respect.”

lines.japanese: やつもまた、非難がましくならないよう注意を払っている感じの答え方だった。
lines.english: Her answer, too, sounded carefully composed to avoid accusation.

lines.japanese: 「アムスとこっち行ったり来たりで、ぜんぜん家のことには興味ないみたいですけどー。だから母も兄も出ていったんじゃないですかねー、まー、父の話を極端にしたがらないのでよく分かんないんですけどー」
lines.english: “He goes back and forth between Amsterdam and here, and he seems entirely uninterested in anything at home. Maybe that's why my mother and brother left. They both avoid talking about him so completely that I don't really know.”

lines.japanese: そう言ってから、鳴は暇をもてあますようにコートを引っぱって皺を伸ばした。
lines.english: After saying it, Naru tugged idly at her coat and smoothed out the wrinkles.

lines.japanese: 俺は返す言葉を探しながら、またテーブルに頬杖をついた。
lines.english: I put my cheek in my hand again while searching for something to say.

lines.japanese: 気付けばいつの間にか、隣りの若い夫婦が席を立っていた。冷めたスープに割り箸が片足突っこんでる。その傍らに、丸めた紙くず。気の抜けたビール。気の抜けた小娘。
lines.english: At some point, the young couple beside us had gone. One chopstick stood ankle-deep in cold soup. Beside it, a ball of paper. Flat beer. A deflated little girl.

lines.japanese: 「出席数だいじょぶかなー」
lines.english: “I wonder if my attendance is still salvageable.”

lines.japanese: 気の抜けた言葉──
lines.english: Deflated words—

lines.japanese: 「やー、こー、いざドロップアウトしかけてみると実感しますねー」
lines.english: “You don’t really feel it until you’re on the verge of dropping out yourself.”

lines.japanese: ──ところがやつはまぶしそうに笑う。
lines.english: —yet she smiled as though dazzled by light.

lines.japanese: 「やっぱり私にも、兄と同じ血が流れてるんだなー、とか」
lines.english: “I really do have the same blood in me as my brother.”

lines.japanese: 「ほー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 俺は頬杖をついたまま、こぶしで顔の皮を引っぱりあげて短い鼻息を吹いた。
lines.english: Still propping up my cheek, I used my fist to drag the skin of my face upward and gave a short snort.

lines.japanese: 「なあ。それは自虐なの、誇りなの」
lines.english: “So is that self-mockery or pride?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、そうですねー。たぶん両方だと思いますよー」
lines.english: “Hmm. Probably both.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: でも野暮な茶々を入れるなら、そんな理屈で括れば世の中なんてこいつらの二親等だらけになってしまう。
lines.english: But to make the graceless objection: by that logic, the world would be overrun with their second-degree relatives.

lines.japanese: だって、放りこまれた輪の中で上手くやれなかったのなんて、そんなのは何もこいつら兄妹だけじゃない。そんな話はそこらじゅうに転がってる。
lines.english: Those two siblings were hardly the only people who had failed to fit into the circle they were thrown into. Stories like that lay everywhere.

lines.japanese: たとえば俺たちの軌跡──
lines.english: Take the course of our own lives—
“Then—”

lines.japanese: 俺の屁理屈みたいな言い分が終わると、じいさんはゆっくりと、凪の湖を漕ぎだすように口を開いた。
lines.english: When my sophistry ran out, the old man slowly began to speak, like a boat setting out across a windless lake.

lines.japanese: 「──先に手を上げたのは君なんだね」
lines.english: “—so you were the one who struck first.”

lines.japanese: 「だから！」
lines.english: “I told you!”

lines.japanese: 俺は長机の上に載せていたエンジニアブーツの踵を浮かせ、すぐに強く叩きつけた。
lines.english: I lifted the heel of the engineer boot propped on the long table and slammed it back down.

lines.japanese: 声変わりも済んで三年。その頃には俺も、ちょっと怒気のこもったでかい音をあげれば、それだけで大抵の大人やガキがたじろぐことを学んでいた──つもりになっていた。
lines.english: My voice had broken three years ago. By then, I had learned—or imagined I had—that merely raising it loud enough with a little anger behind it could make most adults and kids flinch.

lines.japanese: 「てめ、言ってんだろジジイ！　あいつら一年のくせに、タカシんこと何度もパシらせてたんだよ！」
lines.english: “I keep telling you, old man! Those assholes were only first-years, and they kept making Takashi run their errands!”

lines.japanese: 「俺はタカシの為にやってやったの。やつがこれ以上ナメらんねーように！　な、これ復讐！　聖書にもあんだろ？　目には目をって」
lines.english: “I did it for Takashi. So they'd quit treating him like dirt! It was revenge. The Bible has that, right? Eye for an eye.”

lines.japanese: 「それは旧約聖書に曰く、ひとを傷付ければ同じ報いを受けるという意味だ。そして主は、それについてこうおっしゃっている──」
lines.english: “The Old Testament says that whoever injures another shall receive the same injury in return. And concerning that law, the Lord says this—”

lines.japanese: 「いいって。知らねえよ、知ったことか。俺は使徒でも信者でもねえの。俺は俺！」
lines.english: “Enough. Don't know, don't care. I'm no apostle and no believer. I'm me.”

lines.japanese: 「しかし隼人君、君には言葉があるじゃないか。服従の拒絶に腕力は必要ないはずだ」
lines.english: “But Hayato, you have words. Surely you shouldn’t need violence simply to refuse to submit.”

lines.japanese: 「バーカ、おめ、ぬりぃこと言ってんじゃねえよ。どこの天国の話だ、そりゃ」
lines.english: “Idiot. Don’t feed me that soft shit. What kind of heaven do you think you live in?”

lines.japanese: じいさんと会ってから四度目の春。やつの体はようやく老いの兆候を見せはじめ、片やの俺は、着実に技を修め体を鍛えあげていた。
lines.english: It was the fourth spring since I'd met the old man. At last his body had begun to show its age. I, meanwhile, had steadily honed my skills and built up my body.

lines.japanese: まあ、つまりは恥ずかしい話、かなり調子くれてたんだ。説教されんのが嫌なら、会いに行かなきゃいいだけなのにな──いや、仕方ない。何しろ当時の俺にはたったひとりの話相手だ。
lines.english: Which meant, embarrassingly, that I had grown awfully full of myself. If I hated his sermons, I could simply have stopped visiting him—but no. I couldn't. Back then, he was the only person I had to talk to.

lines.japanese: 寂しがり屋のくせにクソ生意気。ついでに言えば無信仰。そんな一銭の得にもならないガキを、あいつはよくもまあ、辛抱強く相手してたもんだ。ほんと大したじいさんだったよ。
lines.english: Lonely as hell, insolent as hell, and an unbeliever besides. It was remarkable how patiently he put up with a kid who wasn't worth a single yen to him. He really was one hell of an old man.

lines.japanese: 「隼人君、新約聖書にはこういう言葉もある。『汝の敵を愛し、迫害するもののために祈れ』」
lines.english: “Hayato, the New Testament also says: ‘Love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you.’”

lines.japanese: 「ムリムリ、ムリムリ」
lines.english: “Can't. No way. Can't, can't.”

lines.japanese: 俺は吹きだしながら片手をひらひら振った。
lines.english: I burst out laughing and flapped one hand in dismissal.

lines.japanese: 「え、じゃあ何か？　俺があの、教師でも目を逸らすようなクソどもにアイラブユーって囁けば、あいつらはタカシから巻きあげた金を返して、握手してキスしてケツの穴まで差しだすってのか？」
lines.english: “What, then? If I whisper ‘I love you’ to those bastards even the teachers won't look in the eye, they'll return the money they shook out of Takashi, shake my hand, kiss me, and offer up their assholes too?”

lines.japanese: 「この言葉の本質はそういうことではないんだ。いいかい──」
lines.english: “That is not the essence of the teaching. Listen—”

lines.japanese: 「あー、いい、いい。そーゆー清らかな夢見事、俺ノーサンキュー。日曜日にゾロゾロ湧いてくる暇なお客さんにだけ語っててくんない」
lines.english: “No, no, spare me. I don't want your pure little fairy tales. Save them for the bored customers who swarm in here every Sunday.”

lines.japanese: 「それよりさー、どうよ最近。鷲介とか、なんか俺のこと言ってた？　俺、しばらくあの馬鹿と≪面談≫してないんだよねー」
lines.english: “More to the point, how've things been? Shusuke say anything about me? I haven't had an *Interview* with that idiot in a while.”

lines.japanese: 俺は机の上の脚を組みかえて、両手を頭の後ろに置いた。
lines.english: I recrossed my legs atop the table and laced my hands behind my head.

lines.japanese: じいさんはしばらく説法を再開する隙をうかがって口を開けたままにしていたが、相手に聞く気がないと分かってゆっくり首を振った。
lines.english: For a while, the old man kept his mouth open and watched for an opportunity to resume his sermon. When he realized I had no intention of listening, he slowly shook his head.

lines.japanese: 「失望という言葉は嫌いだが……もどかしいよ、隼人君」
lines.english: “I dislike the word *disappointment*... but you frustrate me, Hayato.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「初めに言ったはずだが、私は君の中に垣間見た攻撃衝動が、抑圧によって育まれないよう願ってきた。覚えているかな、唯一そのために、自衛のすべを身に付けさせたんだ」
lines.english: “I told you at the beginning. I hoped the aggressive impulse I glimpsed in you would not be fed by repression. Do you remember? That was the sole reason I taught you to defend yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？　じいさん日本語喋れよ」
lines.english: “Huh? Speak plain Japanese, old man.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだァ、おう？　俺は期待に添えなかったのか？　あー、悪かったなそりゃ。ごめんごめん」
lines.english: “What, then? Didn't live up to your expectations? Well, sorry about that. Sorry, sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「でもさー、それって俺が悪いっつーより、あんたに見る目がなかっただけじゃねーの。ぶはは」
lines.english: “But maybe that's less my fault than yours for being a lousy judge of character. Ha!”

lines.japanese: 神聖な空間にクソガキの嘲笑が響くと、じいさんは目蓋を伏せてひとつ小さな息をついた。
lines.english: The sacred space rang with a brat's sneer. The old man lowered his eyelids and let out one small breath.

lines.japanese: 厳粛に威儀を正したようにも見えたし、眼下の卑俗なふるまいに呆れきったようにも見えた。
lines.english: Perhaps he was solemnly gathering his clerical dignity. Perhaps the vulgar performance beneath his gaze had exhausted him.

lines.japanese: でももしかしたら（今にして思うんだけど）、俺のあまりのガキっぷりに漏れかけた苦笑を、はりつけのおっさんに隠れて押し殺していたのかもしれない。
lines.english: Or perhaps—and this occurred to me only much later—my sheer childishness had almost made him smile, and he had ducked behind the man on the cross to choke it back.

lines.japanese: じいさんは目を開けると、おもむろに頭を垂れ、ぶら下げていた首飾りを体の外へと通した。
lines.english: The old man opened his eyes, deliberately bowed his head, and drew the necklace up and off.

lines.japanese: 銀色の十字架は首から右手へ、そしてじいさんのポケットへと素早く移送されていった。
lines.english: The silver cross traveled swiftly from his neck to his right hand and into his pocket.

lines.japanese: 「おい、クソ坊主」
lines.english: “Listen here, you little shit.”

lines.japanese: 瞬間、やつの目が一気に三十ぐらい若返ったように見えた。
lines.english: In that instant, his eyes seemed to shed thirty years.

lines.japanese: やばい。と思ったときにはもう遅かった。飛びこんでくる肌色の弾丸は確かに見切れたけど、罰当たりな俺はあまりに体勢が悪すぎた。
lines.english: *Oh, shit.* By the time I thought it, I was too late. I saw the flesh-colored bullet coming clearly enough, but my blasphemous posture could hardly have been worse.

lines.japanese: 右の顎に素手の拳骨が突きささった。俺は体ごと長椅子に倒され、そのままずるりと床へ滑りおちた。
lines.english: A bare fist buried itself in the right side of my jaw. It toppled me bodily onto the pew, and from there I slid to the floor.

lines.japanese: 老獪な一発は、重みこそ足りないものの的確に急所を捕え、ダメージ以上に俺の脳を揺さぶった。刹那の暗闇に星が爆ぜた。机と椅子の狭い隙間で、俺は痛みと衝撃に目を回していた。
lines.english: The seasoned punch lacked weight but found the vital point with perfect accuracy, rattling my brain far beyond the damage it dealt. Stars burst across an instant of darkness. Wedged in the narrow gap between table and pew, I reeled with pain and shock.

lines.japanese: 「つっ……て、ンめぇ……」
lines.english: “Ghh... you... bastard...”

lines.japanese: 長机の下から無様に這いでて膝を立てると、待ちかまえていたじいさんの二発目がボディに埋めこまれた。
lines.english: I crawled ignominiously from beneath the long table and rose to one knee. The old man was waiting; his second punch sank into my gut.

lines.japanese: 「うっ」
lines.english: “Ugh.”

lines.japanese: 俺はやつの足元でうずくまり、肺に空気を送りこみながら激しく毒づいた。
lines.english: Curled at his feet, I cursed him savagely while forcing air back into my lungs.

lines.japanese: 「の……クソが！」
lines.english: “You... piece of shit!”

lines.japanese: 「ナマクラ坊主っ……！　てめえ！　てめえ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ！」
lines.english: “You worthless priest...! I'll—I'll fucking kill you, asshole!”

lines.japanese: 「聞こえとるよ、小僧。いくら俺が年寄りだからって、いちいちそんなでかい声を張りあげてくれるな。漁師でもないのに気の荒い男は、いつまで経っても女にもてんぞ」
lines.english: “I can hear you, boy. I may be old, but you needn’t shout every word at me. A man with that foul a temper when he isn’t even a fisherman will never win a woman, no matter how long he lives.”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ！？　んだコラ、やんのかテメェ！」
lines.english: “What!? You wanna go, asshole?”

lines.japanese: 幼稚な恫喝に、老人は表情をほころばせて静かに言いかえした。
lines.english: At my childish threat, the old man's expression softened, and he quietly repeated himself.

lines.japanese: 「聞こえなかったのか？　俺は声を荒げるなと言ったぞ」
lines.english: “Did you not hear me? I told you not to raise your voice.”

lines.japanese: 「ふむ……まずその怒鳴り癖が良くないのは、俺が聖職者に向いてないことよりも明らかだな。よし、こうしよう。おまえさん今日から、怒鳴ったりがなったりは禁止だ」
lines.english: “Hmm... First, that habit of shouting is plainly no good—plainer even than the fact that I’m unfit for the clergy. Very well. From today onward, you are forbidden to shout or bellow.”

lines.japanese: 「あァッ！？」
lines.english: “What!?”

lines.japanese: 「しかし、そうだな、たしかに俺はごちゃごちゃと持って回った『夢見事』を並べすぎた。そういうのは鷹志か鷲介にでも話しておこう」
lines.english: “Still, you are right: I have burdened you with too many roundabout ‘fairy tales.’ I shall save those for Takashi or Shusuke.”

lines.japanese: 「いいか隼人。いま、おまえに訓えるのはただ一言。とても明快な一言だ」
lines.english: “Listen, Hayato. I will teach you only one thing now. One very simple thing.”

lines.japanese: じいさんは皺だらけのざらざらした、でもあったかい手で、俺の体を力強く引っぱりおこした。
lines.english: With a hand that was wrinkled and rough but warm, the old man hauled me firmly to my feet.

lines.japanese: 「怒るな──それだけだ。分かるな？　いかなるときも心を平静に保ち動ずることなかれだ」
lines.english: “Do not grow angry. That is all. Do you understand? Whatever happens, preserve your peace of mind and remain unshaken.”

lines.japanese: 「なに、戸惑うことはない。大丈夫だ、可愛い坊主。おまえならきっと出来る」
lines.english: “There's no need to be confused. You'll be all right, my dear boy. I know you can do it.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、つうか……」
lines.english: “No, I mean...”

lines.japanese: 「いまの一言じゃねーじゃん」
lines.english: “That was a hell of a lot more than one sentence.”
